notes:
Nineteen turns. The fragment opens exactly on a bold label — "Sr. PRESIDENTE.- Queda aprobada la resolución", the close of item 9 — so it is not cut mid-speech and that turn is listed. THE LABEL WELDED TO A HEADING — the worst thing in this fragment. After the prosecretary's "(Lee:)" for item 14, the page prints one
block whose bold run reads, with no space and no separator: Orden del Día N° 1230Sr. PRESIDENTE.- and then leaves the bold run for "En consideración en general." So the title of the report being read and the president's next speaker label are fused into a single bold string inside a single centred block, and there is no

anywhere near it. I verified this against the raw file (data/raw/senado/taquigraficas/1998-11-18_r58_ORDINARIA.html, around byte 78213) to be sure it is the chamber's own botch and not an artefact of how the stretch was sliced. It is not. I split it the only way it can be read: "Orden del Día N° 1230" is the heading of the inserted report, "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-" is a real label, and the president's turn runs on through "Tiene la palabra el señor presidente de la Comisión de Asuntos Constitucionales, a quien en este momento no veo en el recinto..." and "Estamos a la espera del señor senador Yoma...". Any parser that anchors a label to the start of a paragraph, or that requires whitespace before "Sr.", will swallow this turn whole. Note also that the report announced by that heading is never reproduced — the prosecretary's "(Lee:)" is followed straight by the title and then by the president. The same happens at item 10, where the reading is represented only by the italic note "-Se lee el proyecto de declaración que figura en el punto ... de los Asuntos Entrados." (the ellipsis is the typist's; the point number was never filled in). Both readings are the prosecretary's own turns, per rule 3, and I invented no speaker for the documents. WHAT COUNTS AS A START. As in my other stretches, I listed every printed bold label, including the president resuming after only a vote note or a section break. Read strictly, rule 2 would merge those, but here that would collapse items 10 through 14 into about three enormous turns and erase the boundaries between five separate pieces of business. The starts a stricter reading would drop are, in my numbering, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16. Turn 16 is the closest call in the fragment: "-Luego de unos instantes:" is plainly an interruption inside a single stretch of presiding, and the president had already said "Estamos a la espera del señor senador Yoma" before it. I still listed it, because the label is printed. TYPIST'S ERRORS RECORDED AS PRINTED, per rule 4: turn 11 reads "Corresponde pasa a cuarto intermedio" (for "pasar"); turn 5 ends "se va a votar" with no full stop, and turn 9's equivalent line reads "se va votar" with the "a" missing. Turn 14's label is shouted — "SR. PROSECRETARIO" — where turn 4's is "Sr. PROSECRETARIO"; same man, same sitting, and I did not tidy either. Every president label in this fragment is bare "Sr. PRESIDENTE.-" with no holder named. MARKUP TRAPS. (a) The section numbers and titles are in

blocks that are NOT preceded by a

, and they follow the previous paragraph's directly. (b) Item 14's block is preceded by an empty

. (c) Turn 13's label nests the other way round from all the others — Sr. PRESIDENTE.- rather than .... (d) Turn 11's label has no space before the text: "Sr. PRESIDENTE.- Corresponde". None of these change what is printed. The cuarto intermedio is the recess to sit as the Tribunal de Juicio Político; "-Son las 19 y 20." and "-A las 19 y 35:" are its opening and closing time stamps and are events, not speech.
